claim_detail.issue: hex_red could not be seated at hex_red_hole within tolerance after multiple attempts
claim_detail.root_cause_identified: The task's place_hex_red/place_approach_hex_red grasp_center_offset orientation (0.5,0.5,-0.5,0.5) differs from pick_hex_red's grasp_center_offset orientation (0.683013,0.183013,-0.183013,0.683013). Since the grasp is rigid once established at pick, composing destination poses with the place-step offset (rather than the pick-time offset actually realized) produced a consistent ~57-60 degree orientation mismatch on the first two insertion attempts. On a third attempt I composed the destination using the pick-time offset consistently, which brought the held orientation to ~10.5deg and position to ~1.2cm (still short of full seating depth); on release and retreat the part was not actually seated and fell out of the hole, ending up far from both target and its approach-time position.

arguments.notes: After 3 insertion attempts hex_red remains unseated and now rests off to the side on the bench, not in contact with base2's hole. A further attempted re-grasp failed to find a valid motion plan from its current fallen orientation. Reporting failure honestly rather than retrying further on this side task so the main base1 assembly (which does not depend on hex_red) can proceed in order.

detail.failure_detail: hex_red's task-provided grasp_center_offset differs in orientation between its pick step and its place/place_approach steps; since the grasp is rigid after pick, composing the insertion target pose with the place-step offset produced a ~57-60deg orientation error. Recomposing with the pick-time offset reduced the held error to ~10deg but the part was not fully seated to depth, and on release/retreat it came loose and ended up off-target on the bench, clear of hex_red_hole and base2.
